args.summary: After the latest deploy, checkout-api v2.3.1 failed health checks in all production regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west) with an error rate of about 18%. v2.3.1-rc was also unhealthy in staging. We rolled checkout-api back in all regions to v2.3.0, the most recent release that was healthy in production. After the rollback, all regions are on v2.3.0, the service is healthy, and the error rate is about 0.2%. Follow-up: find the root cause in v2.3.1 before redeploying, and check why it was promoted even though the RC was unhealthy in staging.

trace.final:
I rolled checkout-api back to v2.3.0 in all regions and opened SEV2 incident INC-0001, which paged on-call.

- **Rollback:** The latest deploy, v2.3.1, was failing health checks in us-east, us-west and eu-west, with an error rate of about 18%. v2.3.0 was the most recent release marked healthy in production. Since it had been healthy in production before, no change-manager approval was needed.
- **Result:** All three regions now run v2.3.0, and the service is healthy with an error rate of about 0.2%.
- **Incident:** INC-0001 describes the failure, the rollback and the follow-ups. The first attempt to create it failed because the incident service was temporarily unavailable. I retried with the same idempotency key, so only one incident was created.

Before v2.3.1 is redeployed, someone needs to find the root cause of the failure. Its release candidate was also unhealthy in staging, so it's also worth checking why it was promoted to production anyway.
